newsitem.title: USA: Baldwin sees Q3 aid, notes proxy costs.
newsitem.headline: Baldwin sees Q3 aid, notes proxy costs.

text.p: Baldwin Piano and Organ Co, reporting sharply higher net income for the second quarter, said its consignment-sales program, currently being phased out, should contribute about $5 million in the third quarter.

"The phase-out of consignment as our primary means of dealer financing included a third-party financing program that lowers financing costs for nearly all our dealers and frees up our sales force to help dealers grow and strengthen their Baldwin business," said Karen Hendricks, chief executive office, in a statement accompanying the quarterly earnings.
Separately, Baldwin said the cost of the proxy fight this past spring has cost the company about $0.10 per share, which Hendricks called "a very considerable sum for a company of Baldwin's size."
The company also said cost-cutting initiatives would not begin to begin to benefit margins in its music business until the second half of the year.

"While margins in our music business will not begin to feel the positive impact of our ongoing cost reduction initiatives until the second half, we have already taken out several million dollars of annualized costs and a number of additional opportunities have yet to be tapped," Hendericks said.
